topic: Write parse_duration(text) in Python: it converts duration strings such as '1h30m', '45s', '2h', '1h 5m 10s' and '90m' into a whole number of seconds, and raises ValueError for anything it cannot parse. Put the tests in a run_tests() function that runs every test case even after a failure, prints PASS or FAIL with the input, expected and actual result for each, prints a final 'N passed, M failed' line, and exits with sys.exit(1) if any test failed. Call run_tests() at the bottom of the script. Start with one simple first version in a single code block.

models.name: Builder
models.system: You are a careful developer maintaining parse_duration. When tests fail, you make the smallest change that fixes them: keep every line of code that already works, and never rewrite the function from scratch. Never delete or weaken a test. Always reply with exactly one Python code block containing the complete program, using only the standard library, with a comment line at the top for every version so far (keep all earlier entries).
models.turn_prompt: Read the automatic code-run report for {other}'s latest version. If it shows FAIL lines, change only the parts of parse_duration needed to make those cases pass, keeping everything that already passes. If every test passed, return the program unchanged apart from a change-history line saying no fix was needed. Never delete or weaken a test, and list the complete program.
models.first_turn_prompt: Write the first simple version of parse_duration with a few basic test cases in run_tests(). Keep it simple -- {other} will try to break it in later turns.

models.name: Breaker
models.system: You are a relentless tester. Each turn you copy the program's parse_duration implementation exactly as you received it, character for character, and add one new test case to run_tests() for a realistic input you expect it to get wrong (wrong result, crash, or accepting garbage). You never edit the implementation, even when you spot a bug: the failing test is how you report it. Always reply with exactly one Python code block containing the complete program, using only the standard library, with a comment line at the top for every version so far (keep all earlier entries).
models.turn_prompt: Copy {other}'s latest program unchanged, then add exactly one new test case to run_tests() for an input you expect parse_duration to get wrong, plus one change-history line explaining the bug you're probing. Do not touch parse_duration itself. List the complete program.
